![](figures/figureS_alad_cohort/figureS_alad_cohort.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label alad-cohort >}}.
ALAD cohort, RISE factor matrices, and collinearity and stability of RISE and CPD components.** ({{< panel alad-cohort cohort >}}) Schematic of the ALAD cohort data\ [@doi:10.1016/j.healun.2024.02.007].
({{< panel alad-cohort factors genes >}}) RISE factor matrices representing component loadings of conditions and genes; conditions are grouped by ALAD status, then six-month outcome (color strips).
For visualization, genes outside the top 10% by weight in any component are omitted and each component is normalized to its largest absolute loading.
({{< panel alad-cohort cp-collinearity >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the condition, sender, receiver, and LR pair factors of any two CPD components across ranks, as the median (line and points) and interquartile range (band; IQR) over 10 seeded SVD starts per rank.
({{< panel alad-cohort rise-fms >}}) RISE gene factor and ({{< panel alad-cohort cpd-fms >}}) CPD LR pair factor FMS of each component across leave-one-patient-out jackknife replicates (n = 45), and, right of the dashed line, the aggregate FMS (mean over components) of each jackknife and re-initialization (seed only, n = 100) replicate.
Each replicate's components were matched to the reference's by Hungarian matching.
Boxes show the median and IQR and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the IQR.

![](figures/figureS_ibd_rank_selection/figureS_ibd_rank_selection.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label ibd-rank-selection >}}.
IBD rank selection.** ({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cohort >}}) Schematic of the IBD cohort data\ [@doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02634-7].
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection rise-rank-selection >}}) RISE R^2^X across ranks of the fit on all data and, in BiCV, of the fit on the training block (BiCV train) and its prediction of the held-out block (BiCV test); mean ± SD over 10 repeats per rank.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection bicv-test >}}) BiCV test R^2^X from ({{< panel ibd-rank-selection rise-rank-selection >}}) on its own magnified axis.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-r2x-starts >}}) CPD fit R^2^X across ranks: the median (line) and range (band) over 10 seeded SVD starts per rank.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-collinearity >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the LR pair factors of any two CPD components across ranks, for each start (points), colored by whether the start reaches the solution most starts reach at its rank (blue) or another solution (grey).
Boxes show the median and IQR and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the IQR.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-minima >}}) Number of the 10 starts reaching each distinct solution across ranks (starts joined at FMS ≥ 0.95): the solution most starts reach (blue, bottom) and each other solution (grey), colored as in ({{< panel ibd-rank-selection cp-collinearity >}}).
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection mode-collinearity >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the condition, sender, and receiver factors of any two CPD components across ranks, as the median (line and points) and IQR (band) over the starts.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection factors genes >}}) RISE factor matrices at the selected rank representing component loadings of conditions and genes.
({{< panel ibd-rank-selection eigenstate-heatmap >}}) RISE cell-type--eigen-state associations derived from RISE rank-60 projection matrices: mean RISE projection of each cell type's cells onto each eigen-state.

![](figures/figureS_ibd_associations/figureS_ibd_associations.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label ibd-associations >}}.
Association of CPD components and covariates with IBD biopsy type.** ({{< panel ibd-associations cp-associations >}}) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each CPD component's condition loadings against each IBD biopsy categorization.
\*: q < 0.05, Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) corrected across all categorizations and components.
({{< panel ibd-associations status-loadings >}}) CPD component ({{< panel ibd-associations status-loadings.1 >}}) 3 and ({{< panel ibd-associations status-loadings.2 >}}) 4 condition loadings by CD inflammation status.
Violins show the distribution of loadings, points show individual biopsies, and ticks mark the median.
One-way ANOVA F and η^2^, with p BH corrected across all categorizations and components.
({{< panel ibd-associations lineage-proportions >}}) Fraction of each biopsy's cells in each coarsely annotated cell type for healthy, CD uninflamed, and CD inflamed samples, on a square-root scale.
Boxes show the median and IQR and whiskers show the most extreme values within 1.5-times the IQR.
q: Kruskal--Wallis test across the three groups, BH corrected across cell types.
({{< panel ibd-associations covariates >}}) One-way ANOVA η^2^ of each biopsy covariate and coarse cell-type fraction against each biopsy categorization, with binary covariates coded 0/1.
\*: p < 0.05, uncorrected.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_rank_selection/figureS_comparator_rank_selection.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-rank-selection >}}.
Rank selection of the label-based comparators.** Each method's own rank selection on coarse and fine labels, ALAD and IBD together.
Dashed lines mark each cohort's chosen rank, and red circles mark the Kneedle elbow.
PB, pseudobulk CPD; TC2C, Tensor-cell2cell; STAC, STACCato.
({{< panel comparator-rank-selection pb-fit-coarse pb-fit-fine >}}) PB fit R^2^X across ranks, over 10 seeded SVD starts per rank.
Lines show the median and bands the range over starts.
({{< panel comparator-rank-selection tc2c-elbow-coarse tc2c-elbow-fine >}}) TC2C normalized reconstruction error across ranks, over 10 random starts per rank.
Lines show the mean and bands the range.
({{< panel comparator-rank-selection pb-collinearity-coarse pb-collinearity-fine >}}) Largest absolute cosine between the LR pair factors of any two PB components, over the same starts as ({{< panel comparator-rank-selection pb-fit-coarse pb-fit-fine >}}).
Median and range, as in ({{< panel comparator-rank-selection pb-fit-coarse pb-fit-fine >}}).
({{< panel comparator-rank-selection tc2c-congruence-coarse tc2c-congruence-fine >}}) Largest congruence product between any two components of a TC2C start, over the same starts as ({{< panel comparator-rank-selection tc2c-elbow-coarse tc2c-elbow-fine >}}).
Median and range.
({{< panel comparator-rank-selection pb-minima-coarse pb-minima-fine >}}) PB and ({{< panel comparator-rank-selection tc2c-minima-coarse tc2c-minima-fine >}}) TC2C share of a rank's starts that reach its most common solution.
Starts are counted as one solution when their FMS is at least 0.95.
({{< panel comparator-rank-selection stac-shares-coarse stac-shares-fine >}}) STAC eigenvalue share of each component of each mode's unfolding.
The dashed line marks the 1% cutoff.
Cores are given as condition × LR pair × sender × receiver.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_ibd_and_depth/figureS_comparator_ibd_and_depth.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-ibd-and-depth >}}.
Comparator recovery of the IBD components, and detection depth in every method's components.** PB, pseudobulk CPD; TC2C, Tensor-cell2cell; STAC, STACCato; C and F, coarse and fine labels.
({{< panel comparator-ibd-and-depth ibd-best >}}) Largest cos^2^ between the LR pair loadings of each IBD CCC-RISE component (n = 6) and any single LR column of each comparator fit.
({{< panel comparator-ibd-and-depth ibd-containment >}}) Fraction of each IBD CCC-RISE component's LR pair loadings reconstructed by the best combination of all LR columns of each comparator fit.
({{< panel comparator-ibd-and-depth depth >}}) Absolute Spearman correlation between the absolute condition loadings of each CCC-RISE component or comparator LR column and the median number of genes detected per cell, computed across samples (ALAD, n = 47) or biopsies (IBD, n = 343).
Each point is one component or column (ALAD, n = 58; IBD, n = 40), grouped by fit.
For STAC columns, the condition loadings are the leading vector of each LR component's core slice, mapped through the condition factor.
Boxes show the median and IQR, and whiskers show the full range.
Kruskal--Wallis test across the fits of each cohort: ALAD, p = 1 × 10^−5^; IBD, p = 1 × 10^−4^.
A star marks a fit whose components track depth more than the cohort's other components.
This uses a one-sided Mann--Whitney U test with BH correction across the fits of the cohort, given a Kruskal--Wallis p below 0.05.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_missed_alad/figureS_comparator_missed_alad.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-missed-alad >}}.
Comparator LR columns that are not part of a CCC-RISE component in ALAD.** PB, pseudobulk CPD; STAC, STACCato; C and F, coarse and fine labels.
LR columns are named by method (P, S) and number, and top LR pairs are as in {{< fig 5 >}}.
({{< panel comparator-missed-alad share >}}) Share of each PB and STAC LR column's squared LR pair loading that falls on the top LR pairs of one CCC-RISE component.
n = 39 columns.
The dashed line marks 0.5.
Eighteen columns fall below it.
({{< panel comparator-missed-alad associations >}}) Each column's strongest association with an ALAD outcome grouping, as effect size (η^2^) against q, beside the CCC-RISE components that have an association with q < 0.05 (blue).
One-way ANOVA across samples (n = 47), with BH correction across all nine groupings and all components of each fit.
The panel draws the eight groupings other than acute rejection.
The dashed line marks q = 0.05.
The box lists, for each grouping, the columns and CCC-RISE components with q < 0.05.
({{< panel comparator-missed-alad contents >}}) Top LR pairs of the 18 columns below 0.5 in ({{< panel comparator-missed-alad share >}}), sized by absolute loading relative to the column's largest.
The CCC-RISE row shows each LR pair's largest such value in any CCC-RISE component.
Bold names and red boxes mark the columns with q < 0.05 in ({{< panel comparator-missed-alad associations >}}) that carry a top LR pair outside every CCC-RISE component's top LR pairs whose ligand and receptor are different genes.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_missed_ibd/figureS_comparator_missed_ibd.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-missed-ibd >}}.
Comparator LR columns that are not part of a CCC-RISE component in IBD.** As in {{< fig comparator-missed-alad >}}, for IBD.
H, healthy; CD, Crohn's disease; U and I, CD uninflamed and inflamed.
({{< panel comparator-missed-ibd share >}}) Share of each LR column's squared LR pair loading on the top LR pairs of one CCC-RISE component (n = 28 columns).
Fifteen columns fall below 0.5.
({{< panel comparator-missed-ibd associations >}}) Each column's strongest association with a biopsy grouping.
One-way ANOVA across biopsies (n = 343), with Benjamini--Hochberg correction across all three groupings and all components of each fit.
The panel draws H vs. CD and U vs. I. ({{< panel comparator-missed-ibd contents >}}) Top LR pairs of the 15 columns below 0.5 in ({{< panel comparator-missed-ibd share >}}), sized by absolute loading relative to the column's largest.
The CCC-RISE row shows each LR pair's largest such value in any CCC-RISE component.
Bold names and red boxes mark the columns with q < 0.05 in ({{< panel comparator-missed-ibd associations >}}) that carry a top LR pair outside every CCC-RISE component's top LR pairs whose ligand and receptor are different genes.

![](figures/figureS_comparator_single_cell/figureS_comparator_single_cell.svg){width="6.5in"}

**{{< label comparator-single-cell >}}.
Single-cell comparison of CCC-RISE populations.** ({{< panel comparator-single-cell scriabin-seeds >}}) Agreement between random seeds, measured as the mean best-match Jaccard index between two seeds' LR sets.
Scriabin's LR sets are its interaction programs whereas CCC-RISE's are its components' top LR pairs.
Each point is a pair of seeds, and bars mark medians.
Scriabin: 10 seeds, n = 45 pairs in each cohort.
CCC-RISE: 10 refits in ALAD (n = 45 pairs) and 5 in IBD (n = 10 pairs).
({{< panel comparator-single-cell alad-weights >}}) ALAD and ({{< panel comparator-single-cell ibd-weights >}}) IBD per-cell sender weight against receiver weight on each CCC-RISE component, each relative to its largest value (ALAD, n = 51,273 cells; IBD, n = 634,534 cells).
Dashed lines mark the 0.3 cutoff (τ) that defines each component's sender, receiver and both populations.
({{< panel comparator-single-cell alad-tau >}}) ALAD and ({{< panel comparator-single-cell ibd-tau >}}) IBD fraction of NICHES+ cells in each sender (solid) and receiver (dotted) population, minus the fraction predicted by cell type as in {{< fig 5 niches-fraction >}}, across cutoffs τ from 0.1 to 0.6.
A population is drawn only while it has at least 10 cells.
The grey line marks the 0.3 cutoff used throughout, and the dashed line marks no difference.

{{< include figures/tables/alad_outcome_groups.md >}}

**{{< label alad-outcome-groups >}}.
ALAD samples by outcome group.** Number of BAL samples in each ALAD status and six-month outcome group the analyses compare.
Indented groups are subgroups of the group above them.
Two of the 45 patients were sampled twice, in different groups.
